newsitem.title: UK: Poll shows support for UK anti-corruption candidate.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows support for UK anti-corruption candidate.

text.p: Britain's anti-corruption candidate in the May 1 election has considerable support among voters, according to a poll on Tuesday.

A MORI poll of 500 voters for ITN's News At Ten showed that 55 percent supported BBC war correspondent Martin Bell's decision to stand against former Conservative minister Neil Hamilton who is a the centre of a parliamentary ethics probe.
Twenty-two percent said he should not stand.

Hamilton, who has denied allegations that he accepted money from a businessman in exchange for asking questions in parliament, received the backing of his local party to stand as the Conservative candidate for the Tatton seat in northwest England that he won by a large majority in 1992.
"Seventy-two percent said the allegations of misconduct were important in deciding how to vote, with 42 percent of them saying it was very important," ITN said in a statement.

MORI interviewed 463 people from a panel of 500 electors in the six marginal constituencies of Bury North, Coventry South, Exeter, Basildon, Edinburgh, Pentlands and Conwy in Wales by telephone on Tuesday.
